notes:
Two fixes that each began as something smaller, and the first working regression tests.

CREDENTIALS ARE KEYED BY SERVER, NOT BY SHARE. Started as a way to let automated tests drop and re-add a share without a password being typed — Claude will not enter credentials, and that constraint does not move. The intended workaround (keep a second permanent share so credentials survive) turned out not to work, for a reason that WAS the bug: KeychainCredentialStore filed secrets under the share's sourceId, so removing the last share on a server orphaned them under a key nothing could look up again. Re-adding minted a fresh UUID, missed, and asked for a password the app was still holding. Adding a share to a SURVIVING server worked, because a live source row was there to read from, which is why it looked intermittent. Now keyed per server (CredentialKey.forHost — lowercased, trailing .local stripped). Migration v21 re-files ADDITIVELY: a half-finished keychain move would lock a user out of their own NAS with no recovery, and resolvedCredentials' fallback tier still answers from the old key. Verified end to end — migration re-filed, a change check logged into the NAS, the share was removed, re-added, and the credentials screen came up prefilled and authenticated with nothing typed. Removing a SHARE now keeps credentials; removing a SERVER forgets them, which is the only unambiguous statement of intent.

ARTWORK: THE COVER WAS CREED. Tom asked whether the 'greatest hits' guard he remembered existed. It did not — what existed was blast-radius containment added 2026-07-27 (the online pass demoted to gap-filling, so a wrong match can never overwrite correct folder art). Matching itself had no verification at all: limit=1, results.first taken on faith, artistName never read. Johnny Cash's '18 Greatest Hits' was carrying CREED's greatest hits, found by opening the JPEG. The old query reproduced it live that morning, having returned Al Green in July.

Fixed structurally rather than by tuning the query. New ArtworkLookup resolves the ARTIST first, then searches only that artist's catalogue, so a wrong-artist match stops being expressible. artistId caches per artist, making it cheaper than the old single-call version on any real library. Threshold 0.62 set from measurement across eight albums (correct matches 0.75+, wrong ones 0.57 and below). '18 Greatest Hits' is not in Apple's catalogue at all, so it now gets NO artwork rather than wrong artwork.

THE UNIT TESTS EARNED THEIR KEEP BEFORE SHIPPING. Containment was scored symmetrically, so 'Greatest' sitting inside '18 Greatest Hits' scored 0.75 — an album titled Greatest would have been auto-accepted. The live API strings hid it behind '(feat. The Tennessee Two)' suffixes. Containment is now asymmetric: a candidate containing the whole wanted title scores high, a fragment falls through to token overlap.

FIRST REGRESSION TESTS THAT RUN. tools/tests/ — runner, harness, and the scan suite. One test runs fully unattended and was mutation-validated: staling a single folder fingerprint produced 'files planned for an unchanged library: expected 0, got 12' in four seconds, which is the guard against folder fingerprinting regressing into rescan-everything. Two tests are written but SKIP, because this Mac has no scriptable tap and starting a scan needs a button press. Tom's call on that: XCUITest over idb — given a choice between a third-party dependency and none, take none — and parked until the UI redesign, since coordinates written against the current screens would be thrown away.

FOUND ALONG THE WAY. bEmptyFolderStatsDisablesChangeChecks: with folder_stats empty but scanState complete, lastScanned set and 95 tracks present, the app declares the share 'never scanned' and skips the change check forever — a library that silently stops updating behind a UI that says complete. Produced artificially and logged as such; no natural path found, Backup & Restore named as the place to look. Also confirmed the CD2 disc-tag mismatch is source data, not a scanner fault: the files themselves say [Disc 1] and carry no disc number at all. Left deliberately as the acceptance case for a future library-repair feature.

ARTWORK ROADMAP CAPTURED. Six open items, dependency-ordered, from Tom's direction on a maintenance view that surfaces sub-100% confidence and low-resolution covers. Measured on the way: 4 of 5 albums serve 1200x1200 from the same URL the code asks 600x600 from (fArtworkHigherResolutionFetch, XS), and track-listing overlap is a far stronger signal than title similarity — the title-ranked winner shared 22% of tracks, the one title matching never surfaced shared 78%. Recorded that upscaling is cosmetic and hallucinates text on sleeves, that it must apply to manually-added art and not just scanned art, and — Tom's correction — that upscaling is not core functionality, so a hosted option is a product trade rather than an architectural breach.
